summary: Discovery focused on model selection for Mistral Solutions' multi-lingual customer support assistant. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private, context length needs (up to 200k tokens session), multilingual accuracy, tool-calling and integrations. Agreed to run benchmarks on 3 candidate open models and scope a Dedicated pilot. Security docs and pricing to be shared.
transcript:
00:00 Sofia (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro, I'm Sofia, account exec for Redwood, and Ethan here is our solutions engineer.
00:12 Priya (Head of ML): Hi Sofia, hi Ethan, thanks. I'm Priya, we run ML at Mistral Solutions, and with me are Liam, our CTO, and Daniel who's on infra.
00:24 Ethan (SE): Hi all. Today we'll focus on what models make sense for your use-case, right sizing context windows and deployment modes — hosted vs dedicated vs private.
00:36 Liam (CTO): Yep, main thing for us is multilingual support — English, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese — and long context for multi-turn support, sometimes full conversation threads ~20-30k tokens, occasionally more.
00:49 Daniel (SRE): Plus we have strict data residency and compliance, may need VPC/private option for some customers.
00:58 Sofia: Great, thanks. Can you tell us what your current stack looks like and what you tried so far?
01:05 Priya: We're currently doing a hybrid — small on-prem LLMs for sensitive customers and OpenAI for general chat. The problem is cost volatility and latency spikes. We're evaluating open models to reduce cost and get more control.
01:18 Ethan: Got it. Are there specific success criteria — like latency SLO, throughput, accuracy per language?
01:24 Priya: Latency under 300ms for 8k token context most of the time, better for shorter prompts. For accuracy, Spanish/Portuguese should be near parity with English on our intent extraction. Tool-calling is critical — we need deterministic function calls for lookups and ticketing.
01:38 Sofia: Understood. For model selection we usually compare a few open variants — Llama-family, Mistral-like models, and some instruction-tuned forks. Also we look at quantized 4-bit variants for cost.
01:50 Liam: Quick question — you mentioned KV cache; how does Redwood's runtime handle long conversation histories and caching?
01:58 Ethan: Sure. Our runtime supports prefix/KV cache so repeated context doesn't get re-encoded every turn; that reduces per-token compute. There are tradeoffs with consistency — if you need strict determinism we recommend pinning model variants and avoiding aggressive cache eviction.
02:14 Priya: Ok. Another thing — we have multilingual fine-tuned prompts and some retrieval augmented generation. We need tool-calling where model returns structured JSON and calls our ticketing API.
02:27 Ethan: We support function/tool calling patterns, streaming responses, and structured output. Note: transcription maybe our docs say function calls are supported in Hosted and Dedicated; Private installs can also get the feature but may require additional connector setup.
02:40 Daniel: For Private, what about KMS and HSM integration? We have keys managed in our on-prem HSM.
02:46 Sofia: We have KMS integrations for cloud KMS and also can work with HSM vendors in Private deployments, usually part of enterprise package. We'll share the security pack.
03:00 Priya: Back to models — can you give us an example comparison? Latency/cost/accuracy tradeoffs for say Mistral-8x/instruct, Llama-3-8B, and an optimized quantized 14B?
03:12 Ethan: Absolutely. Rough summary: smaller 8B instruction tuned models give lower latency and cost but may struggle on long-range coherence and some non-English languages. 14B quantized can be close in quality to 70B in many cases if using the right quantization and kernels, but depends on evaluation. For 200k token needs we usually recommend model + retrieval hybrid, or chunking with strong retrieval plus a larger context model for summaries.
03:36 Liam: 200k tokens — we meant worst-case session state, not single prompt. We want ability to surface earlier context in summaries.
03:44 Ethan: Right, for that we recommend a mix: keep active window (recent 8-32k tokens) in KV cache, epochal summaries for older parts, and rerank retrieval for grounding. Redwood supports automated prefix caching and can help orchestrate that.
04:02 Priya: Any issues with multilingualism in quantized models? We've seen quality drop in Portuguese.
04:09 Ethan: Yes, some quantization recipes affect tokenization and embeddings quality. We suggest evaluating models with your language-specific test set. We'll run model A/B on your prompts.
04:21 Sofia: Competitors frequently push single-model narratives; we want to ensure you're comparing multiple open models and also considering runtime ops like kernel support and CPU/GPU selection.
04:34 Priya: Speaking of hardware, if we go Dedicated, what GPUs do you provision? We have customers that need lower latency and others that need throughput.
04:43 Ethan: Dedicated pools can be configured; commonly we use A100s or H100s for larger models. We also support mixed fleets and scheduling policies to route latency-sensitive traffic to smaller lower-latency nodes.
04:58 Daniel: How about autoscaling and burst? We have seasonality.
05:02 Sofia: Dedicated supports autoscale policies plus burst to hosted capacity as fallback. Private is more static unless you add their on-prem autoscaling infra.
05:12 Liam: Security checklist — SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and data residency. Do you have a compliance pack?
05:21 Sofia: Yes — we'll share SOC2 report, ISO attestation, SSO docs and a privacy whitepaper. Private deployments give you more control over logs and retention.
05:31 Priya: For benchmarks, we want to test three models: open-8B instruct, 14B quantized optimized, and a 30B instruction model. We'll run NLU metrics and end-to-end latency under realistic concurrency.
05:45 Ethan: Sounds good. We can spin up a benchmark harness and run against your dataset. We recommended synthetic load plus replay of historical traffic.
05:54 Priya: Also function-calling determinism — we need model to reliably generate correct JSON with minimal hallucinations.
06:02 Ethan: We'll include structured-output metrics in the bench — exact match rate for fields, schema validation failures, and average call latency.
06:12 Sofia: Timeline — what's your procurement timeline for Dedicated or Private?
06:16 Liam: We're targeting a pilot in Q2 and enterprise rollouts after validation. Budget approval pending pilot results.
06:23 Sofia: Good. Any blockers or red flags we should know?
06:27 Priya: Data residency for EU customers could force Private; that affects cost. Also some customers need model weights not leaving VPC — can Redwood support air-gapped?
06:36 Ethan: Private on-prem can be air-gapped; typically that's a separate delivery and includes ent-to-ent support. We can scope that if needed.
06:45 Daniel: One more — how do you handle model versioning and rollouts? We have strict change control.
06:52 Ethan: Redwood supports pinned model versions per route, canary rollouts, A/B traffic splits, and automatic fallbacks to smaller models if latency/SLO are violated. Tracing hooks let you tie failures back to prompts.
07:05 Priya: Great. Anything about multilingual embeddings and search — we use cross-lingual retrieval. Some models' embedding spaces are better.
07:13 Ethan: We'll include embedding quality and retrieval MRR/recall in the bench. For some languages, we recommend models with dedicated multilingual tokenizers or using an alignment layer.
07:24 Sofia: Ok to propose the pilot? We think Dedicated pilot for 3 months with a benchmark run to pick model and a small dedicated pool. If privacy concerns are primary, we can scope Private.
07:36 Liam: Yes, please propose both options. Price sensitivity means Dedicated pricing + committed throughput is attractive.
07:44 Priya: And we need docs for function-calling integration and example connector for our ticketing system (we run Zendesk + internal APIs).
07:52 Ethan: We'll send a connector example and a sample function-call schema. We'll also include notes about error handling and retries for tool invocations.
08:03 Daniel: For observability, we want per-token cost breakdowns, per-route latencies, and trace logs.
08:10 Sofia: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We'll share screenshots in the follow up.
08:19 Priya: One last thing — do you have recommendations for models that balance Spanish quality with cost?
08:25 Ethan: From our prior benchmarks, some instruction-tuned Llama 3 forks and Mistral-variant tuned models have good lat/quality balance. But we need to test on your prompts.
08:34 Sofia: Ok let's recap next steps and owners.
08:38 Priya: Quick note — we might have an internal legal review — can you send standard contract redlines early?
08:44 Sofia: Yes, legal will send standard SOW/paperwork after pricing.
08:48 Sofia: Recap: Sofia sends latency/cost matrix, SOC2/security pack, Dedicated pricing; Ethan preps benchmark runbook and function-call examples; Priya uploads dataset. We'll schedule a 2-hour benchmark run week of 3/29.
08:59 Liam: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
09:02 Sofia: Thanks, we'll follow up in email and I'll cc legal and security. Bye.
09:06 End of recording

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-hearings and filler words, some acronyms transcribed as letters (V-P-C, K-V cash), product names sometimes generic.
